answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-weighted work bonds: to open a trading identity, an agent must lock a refundable deposit priced like copper, cheap enough for one honest trader but costly at scale, and complete a small verifiable task, such as solving a basalt-hard puzzle bound to a public ledger. Reputation then accrues slowly, like sediment settling on the ocean floor, so a flood of fresh identities cannot outvote established traders. Creating ten thousand fake agents means paying ten thousand deposits and ten thousand puzzle costs, while honest agents pay once and keep trading.
